records.quote: Smoke particle size measurements were obtained under low-gravity conditions by overheating several materials typical of those found in spacecraft.
records.derivation: Abstract of Appendix C of the Final Report (the 2009 AIAA paper, listed as 'Paper AIAA-2009-956' in the Publication List on page 31), by the SAME team about the SAME flight. Sentence spans two PDF lines, joined with one space. Source term 'low-gravity'; no g-level stated anywhere; mapped to the controlled term microgravity. 'by overheating' = samples heated, not burned (see R7). test_id: flight tests listed in Appendix A (page 33); does not cover the 1-g ground comparison runs (R4-R6). PDF page numbers here are 1-based file indices (page 43 = printed C-1); page-by-page reading failed, so the PDF was read whole.

records.quote: Smoke particulate produced in low-gravity was found to be typically 50% large in count mean diameter than similar conditions in normal gravity.
records.derivation: Conclusion of Appendix E of the Final Report (the 2008 AIAA paper, 'Paper AIAA-2008-0806' in the Publication List on page 31). Typo '50% large' kept as printed. Sentence spans three PDF lines, joined with single spaces. Source term 'low-gravity'; no g-level stated; mapped to microgravity. The 'normal gravity' half of the sentence refers to the ground comparison tests (R4).

records.quote: One of the major goals of this investigation was to quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity and to relate the droplet size distribution to the smoke generation and smoke transport conditions in the experiment.
records.derivation: Objective statement, not a statement of the test condition (brief rule 3). Source term 'low gravity'; no g-level. Proposed only because the record text is the first source; R1 and R2 state the condition as fact. section=hypothesis ('In a μg environment, ...') is a hypothesis and section=projectType ('Microgravity Investigation') is a category label; neither was proposed.

records.quote: Values of D0.5 were calculated directly from the calibrated signals from the P-Trak and the Ion sensor and are shown in Table 1 for the baseline runs of the 4 solid materials with the percentage increase over the sizes from a comparable test in normal gravity.
records.derivation: Appendix E of the Final Report (2008 AIAA paper). 'D0.5' is printed with a subscript; text layer reads 'D0.5'. Sentence spans four PDF lines, joined with single spaces. Table 1 on the same page is captioned 'Table 1: Count Mean Diameters for Baseline Runs with comparison to 1-g tests.' and gives a '% larger than 1-g' value for Silicone Rubber, Lamp wick and Kapton; the Teflon cell is empty. The sources read give no test ids, dates, atmosphere or pressure for these 1-g tests.

records.derivation: Appendix D of the Final Report (2008 SAE ICES paper 2008-01-2089, header on page 51). States that ground-based 1-g comparison runs were being conducted at the time of writing; corroborates R4. Sentence spans two PDF lines, joined with one space.

records.quote: Once the flight mass loss rates were determined, 1-g operation conditions to produce the same loss were determined.
records.derivation: Says 1-g operating conditions were determined, not explicitly that 1-g smoke measurements were made. In the JSON field there is no space between 'determined.' and the next sentence. Caution: other sentences of this same section=approach use 'near field hardware', 'Far Field Box' and 'combustion event', which do not appear in the Final Report's description of the SAME hardware, and section=experimentHardware reads 'Comparitive Soot Diagnostic Hardware'; this section may partly describe the CSD procedure. ('igniter' in the same section may only name the heater wire: filenames in psi-data/PSI-102/Engineering Documents, not opened, use 'Ignitor Wire Coil Assembly'.) R4 and R5 are the stronger 1-g records.

records.test_id: Appendix A Test Number 1, 5-8, 10, 13, 14, 17, 23-35, 41, 46, 47 (Silicone, Teflon, Lampwick, Kapton)
records.quote: Values of D0.5 were calculated directly from the calibrated signals from the P-Trak and the Ion sensor and are shown in Table 1 for the baseline runs of the 4 solid materials with the percentage increase over the sizes from a comparable test in normal gravity.
records.derivation: The '4 solid materials' are the rows of Table 1 on the same page: Silicone Rubber, Teflon, Lamp wick, Kapton. test_id = the Appendix A rows (page 33) whose Sample Type is Silicone, Teflon, Lampwick or Kapton (25 tests). NOT A FLAME: the samples were heated below the ignition point, not burned. Final Report page 3: 'In order to simulate the detection of a pre-fire overheated-material event, samples were heated to temperatures below the ignition point.' Page 35: 'were pyrolyzed at temperatures below the ignition point'. The record's section=approach speaks of an 'igniter' and a 'combustion event'; the Final Report does not describe ignition for SAME ('igniter' may only name the heater wire: Engineering Documents filenames, not opened, say 'Ignitor Wire Coil Assembly').

records.quote: The samples themselves are composed of five (5) materials: Teflon, Kapton, Silicone, Cellulose and DiButyl Phthalate (which being a liquid, is contained within a small section of cotton lampwick) in small, cylindrical sections, that are wrapped with coils of wire (baseline: stainless steel) that both provides the heat energy to the sample when energized and measures its temperature (by its varying resistance).
records.derivation: Liquid dibutyl phthalate (DBP) held in a solid cotton lampwick; DBP was the reference material. test_id = the Appendix A rows (Final Report page 33) whose Sample Type is DBP (22 tests, including reheats). This is a pre-flight design document (June 2005, Rev A, 'PDR design maturity level' per page 5); the Final Report confirms the flight form on page 3: 'A fifth material, dibutyl-phthalate (DBP) retained in a cotton wick was used as a reference.' NOT A FLAME: the wire coil supplies heat; samples were heated below the ignition point (see R7). Sentence spans five PDF lines, joined with single spaces; page 11 = printed page 7.

records.quote: The SAME tests were performed on board ISS in September and early October of 2007.
records.derivation: Page 24 = printed page 14 (Section 4, Flight Tests). Sentence spans two PDF lines, joined with one space. Platform only; not used for gravity_regime.

records.quote: The system was installed in the Microgravity Science Glovebox, an ISS facility that provides many resources including: containment, power, data, video and uplink commanding.
records.derivation: Page 20 = printed page 10. Sentence spans three PDF lines, joined with single spaces. Platform only; not used for gravity_regime. SHARED_LINEAGE: the caller states SAME-R reuses the SAME hardware; not stated in the sources read.
PSI flight-program label. Consistent with R9 (tests performed on board ISS).

records.quote: For each test, a new sample was moved into place by rotating one of the six sample chambers in the carousel into the flow duct and the sample heating and the flow were synchronized to provide a steady air stream over the sample during the heating interval.
records.derivation: air: oxygen balanced mainly by nitrogen. The sources read do not state the composition of this air. Do not confuse with two other gases in the documents: (1) the 'diluent flow' of the Dynamic Diluter (Baseline doc page 10) and the 'DiluitonGas' in the hardware schematic (Final Report page 20, Figure 4) dilute the smoke sample on its way to the instruments; that gas is not named; (2) GN2 is listed as an MSG fluids resource (Baseline doc page 9) used 'for the experiment process and as systems to power its devices' (page 11); no source read says it flows over the sample. Sentence spans six PDF lines, joined with single spaces; page 21 = printed page 11. SHARED_LINEAGE: same hardware reused by SAME-R per the caller; not stated in the sources read.

not_found.looked_in: Record text, all sections (no pressure). Final Report pages 1-68 (no pressure of the gas around the sample; only the 'MSG vacuum resource' on page 54). Baseline doc pages 1-15: only hardware and supply pressures, not the test atmosphere: GN2 'at nominal 120 psig, reduced to <15 psig by Smoke' (page 9), hoses 'nominally operated at +/- 15 psig' (page 11), MDP '200 psid' and '20 psig' (page 14), and 'the MSG is under a negative pressure' with no value (page 14).

Record text, all sections; Final Report pages 1-68; Baseline doc pages 1-15. No oxygen concentration anywhere. The only oxygen mentions are the Mir 'failure of oxygen generation systems' sentence (e.g. Final Report page 13), unrelated to the test atmosphere.

Record text, all sections; Final Report pages 1-68; Baseline doc pages 1-15. Sample (wire) temperatures were controlled, but no gas temperature is given. The '293 K' on Final Report page 65 is the wall boundary condition of the FDS numerical model of the ISS US Lab (Appendix E), not a SAME test condition. Baseline doc page 9 mentions MSG air cooling with no temperature.
Record text, Final Report pages 1-68, Baseline doc pages 1-15. Only the terms 'low-gravity', 'low gravity', 'microgravity' and 'μg' appear; no g value for the flight tests.

lineage: DAFT (shared instrument): the P-Trak particle counter, SAME's zeroth-moment instrument, was first flown in DAFT. Baseline doc page 8: 'The objective for the risk mitigation experiment, DAFT (Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test), is to provide a microgravity technology demonstration of the P-Trak Ultrafine Particle Counter manufactured by TSI.' Final Report page 9: 'DAFT: Dust Aerosol measurement Feasibility Test, a precursor project of SAME'. SAME-R / SAME-2 (shared hardware and documents): stated by the caller, not by the sources read. A file with the same document title, 'PSI-101_Science Documents_SAME_Baseline Concept Description Document_001 Rev A.pdf', is in psi-data/PSI-101, whose record lists publications on 'Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2' (not opened, not compared byte-for-byte). The PSI-102 folder also holds SAME-2 presentations (not read). CSD: Final Report page 14: 'The measurements were made using smoke generated by overheated spacecraft materials in much the same manner as the CSD experiment however the sample temperature, flow field, and particle aging time were more rigorously controlled.' The PSI-102 record's section=experimentHardware reads 'Comparitive Soot Diagnostic Hardware', and its section=approach uses terms ('near field hardware', 'Far Field Box', 'combustion event') that are absent from the Final Report's description of SAME.
